title: Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS / Myocardial Infarction)
clinical_rationale: Severe acute chest discomfort especially radiating to left arm, neck, or jaw accompanied by autonomic symptoms strongly suggests myocardial ischemia.
recommended_action: Initiate immediate emergency medical services (EMS), administer high-flow oxygen if SpO2 < 90%, perform urgent 12-lead ECG, and prepare emergency cardiology transfer. Halt routine outpatient intake.

title: Hypertensive Emergency / Crisis
clinical_rationale: Extreme blood pressure elevation (Systolic >= 180 and/or Diastolic >= 120 mmHg) with acute symptomatic complaints indicates potential acute target-organ damage.
recommended_action: Stat physician evaluation, repeat blood pressure in both arms, assess neurological and fundoscopic status, and transfer to acute care for controlled intravenous antihypertensive titration.

title: Acute Stroke / Transient Ischemic Attack (FAST Criteria)
clinical_rationale: Sudden onset focal neurological deficits (FAST: Face, Arms, Speech, Time) denote acute cerebrovascular ischemia or intracranial hemorrhage with critical time-to-thrombolysis window.
recommended_action: Establish exact time last known well, immediately mobilize 'Code Stroke' or emergency transport for non-contrast brain CT / MRI. Do not administer oral fluids or medications.

title: Thunderclap Headache / Possible Subarachnoid Hemorrhage or Meningism
clinical_rationale: Hyperacute maximal headache onset ('thunderclap') with or without meningeal irritation (nuchal rigidity) is a classic herald for ruptured aneurysm or acute meningitis.
recommended_action: Emergency neurological and neurosurgical consult, prompt non-contrast head CT and lumbar puncture if indicated. Isolation precautions if meningococcemia suspected.

title: Impending Respiratory Failure / Severe Hypoxemia
clinical_rationale: Critical hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%), severe tachypnea (>30/min), or severe bradypnea (<10/min) indicates respiratory muscle exhaustion and imminent arrest.
recommended_action: Immediately support airway, administer high-flow oxygen, prepare for bag-valve-mask ventilation or endotracheal intubation, and transfer to ICU.

title: Suspected Anaphylaxis / Airway Compromise
clinical_rationale: Rapid onset mucosal angioedema with respiratory compromise and/or hypotension is life-threatening anaphylaxis requiring immediate emergency medical attention.
recommended_action: Stat emergency physician evaluation for impending airway compromise, position supine with legs elevated, maintain airway vigilance, and alert resuscitation team.

title: Acute Surgical Abdomen / Peritoneal Irritation
clinical_rationale: Rigid involuntary guarding and extreme acute abdominal pain indicate visceral perforation, acute peritonitis, or ischemic bowel.
recommended_action: NPO (nil per os / nothing by mouth), place wide-bore IV access, avoid opioid masking until surgeon evaluation, stat surgical consult.

title: Active Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage
clinical_rationale: Frank hematemesis or melena signifies substantial gastrointestinal tract bleeding with imminent hemorrhagic hypovolemia.
recommended_action: Urgent gastroenterology evaluation for endoscopy, IV fluid resuscitation, type and crossmatch blood, stop any NSAIDs or anticoagulant intake.

title: Potential Sepsis / Septic Shock Warning
clinical_rationale: Presence of systemic inflammatory response (fever/tachycardia/tachypnea) coupled with altered mentation or hypotension meets sepsis criteria.
recommended_action: Initiate Sepsis Hour-1 bundle: draw blood cultures, check serum lactate, begin broad-spectrum IV antimicrobials and rapid crystalloid fluid resuscitation.

title: Suspected Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) / Severe Hypoglycemia Crisis
clinical_rationale: Extreme glycemic extremes (<55 or >350 mg/dL) with rapid breathing or cognitive depression indicate life-threatening glycemic decompensation.
recommended_action: Stat emergency physician evaluation for acute glycemic decompensation, assess capillary blood glucose, ketones, and initiate urgent metabolic triage.

title: Acute Emergency Contraindication for Routine Ayush Therapy
clinical_rationale: Under Ministry of Ayush clinical practice guidelines, acute emergencies (trauma, active bleeding, toxic exposure, status epilepticus) are strict contraindications for routine outpatient Ayurvedic treatment and mandate emergency hospital diversion.
recommended_action: Halt outpatient Ayurvedic case-taking. Document emergency triage handoff and redirect patient immediately to emergency department / trauma center.
